title: How Vizrt Education Solutions Prepare Students for Real-World Media Careers

Why This Matters Right Now

The broadcast industry is under increasing pressure to deliver high-quality, low-latency video signals, particularly in live production environments. This pressure is driven by the growing demand for real-time graphics and video production, as well as the need for seamless integration with other broadcast systems and standards. As a result, broadcast engineers, operations leads, and CTOs are constantly looking for ways to improve their workflows, reduce latency, and increase efficiency. The integration of JPEG XS into live graphics production workflows, as announced by Vizrt, is a significant development that addresses these challenges. The use of JPEG XS, a standardized technology compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard, enables the transport of high-quality video signals over IP networks with reduced latency. This is particularly important in live production environments, where frame-accurate video and audio transmission are crucial. By reducing the bitrate required for high-quality video transport, JPEG XS enables the use of lower-bandwidth networks, resulting in reduced transmission costs and a more streamlined workflow. The impact of this development extends beyond the technical realm, as it also has significant implications for the education and training of students in the broadcast industry. By providing education solutions that focus on low-latency signal transport and IP-based broadcast workflows, Vizrt is helping to prepare students for real-world media careers. This is essential, as the broadcast industry is becoming increasingly complex, and students need to be equipped with the skills and knowledge to navigate this complexity.

Under the Hood: How It Actually Works

The integration of JPEG XS into live graphics production workflows involves the use of a standardized technology that is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard. This standard ensures interoperability with other devices and systems that support this standard, making it easier to integrate JPEG XS into existing broadcast workflows. The use of JPEG XS enables the transport of high-quality video signals over IP networks with reduced latency, making it ideal for live production environments. In a typical broadcast workflow, the ingest stage involves the acquisition of video and audio signals, which are then processed and transmitted to the playout stage. The use of JPEG XS can be applied at the processing stage, where the video signals are compressed and transmitted over IP networks. This enables the use of lower-bandwidth networks, resulting in reduced transmission costs and a more streamlined workflow. The playout stage involves the transmission of the video signals to the final destination, such as a television broadcast or online streaming platform. The deployment of JPEG XS in live graphics production requires a network infrastructure that supports the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, with a minimum bandwidth of 1 Gb/s and a maximum latency of 1 ms. Additionally, engineers will need to ensure that their equipment is compatible with the JPEG XS standard and that they have the necessary software and firmware updates to support this technology.

There is also the potential for vendor bias and lock-in, as the use of JPEG XS may require the use of specific equipment and software from certain vendors. This can make it difficult for engineers to integrate JPEG XS into existing workflows, and may require significant investment in new equipment and training.
